pr.title: Keep files that sit among review worktrees out of review prune
pr.head: 2296b28a54456b0c9d70911066651e55f3bdcfe3

summary: Each Projector review checks out the pull request's head in a scratch worktree, a Git worktree under the state directory, at reviews/worktrees/<owner>/<repo>/<pr>/<model-key>/<short-sha>. The model key is the folder name for the model that runs the review, such as claude-opus-5-5. Older releases put worktrees one level higher, at <pr>/<short-sha>, which this summary calls the old layout. project review prune sweeps the worktrees that no review on the machine still needs.

Before this change, prune treated every entry in a pull request's folder that was not a folder holding model worktrees as an old-layout worktree, and its removal helper unlinked files and links. So a summary JSON that a reviewer had saved in a pull request's folder was listed as an old worktree, and prune --apply deleted it.

This change makes prune remove only folders. Each file or symbolic link in a pull request's folder or in a model's folder is listed as kept, with the reason that it is not a worktree. The removal helper refuses anything but a real folder inside the worktrees directory. One case now goes the other way: a folder in a pull request's folder whose name is 12 hex characters and which has lost its .git file is removed whole as an old-layout worktree, unless a review set up on this machine uses that name as its model key.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:

groups.title: Prune removes only folders
groups.kicker: What prune treats as a worktree, and what it now leaves alone
intro: prune walks each pull request's folder under the worktrees directory. For each entry there, it decides whether the entry is an old-layout worktree to remove whole, or a model folder whose worktrees it judges one by one. A worktree's .git file is what marks it as a worktree, because Git writes one into each worktree it creates.

The change adds two helpers. is_folder says whether a path is a real directory and not a link to one. not_a_worktree builds the kept entry that prune lists for a file or a link. prune checks is_folder at both levels, in the pull request's folder and in each model's folder, before it considers an entry for removal.

SHORT_SHA matches a folder name of exactly 12 lowercase hex characters, the length that SHORT gives every worktree name. A matching folder without a .git file was read as a model folder, so prune removed its contents one entry at a time with reasons about a model. It is now removed whole as an old-layout worktree, unless a review's state under prs/ uses that name as its model key.

checks.text: No file or link was deleted in a scratch run of this head's prune with apply. The scratch state held files at every level of the worktrees tree, a dangling link, a link to a file, links to outside folders at the pull request, model, and worktree levels, and a symlinked owner folder that Path.glob walks through. Every file and link stayed. remove_scratch refused the two folders reached through the symlinked owner, because each resolves outside the worktrees directory.

files.note: The sweep in prune, the two new helpers, and the narrowed remove_scratch.

checks.text: A file or a link here, such as a saved summary JSON, is listed as kept and never reaches remove_scratch.

A model key of 12 hex characters with a state.json under prs/ is read as a model folder: a scratch run kept its notes file and removed only its earlier head's worktree. Without a state, the folder goes whole. The merge base already removed every entry in such a folder, files included, so the rule deletes nothing the merge base kept.

setup creates new worktrees at <pr>/<model-key>/<short-sha>, one level below where the 12-hex rule applies, so the rule cannot match a worktree that setup is creating. The lock and state checks for those worktrees are unchanged.
prune is the only caller of remove_scratch, so dropping its branch that unlinked files changes no other path.

files.note: A new test puts a summary JSON, a notes file, a link, and a 12-hex folder without .git among the worktrees, and checks what prune --apply keeps and removes. The old link test becomes a --repo test.

checks.text: With the merge base's review.py, this test fails with FileNotFoundError on the deleted summary-1.json. At this head it passes, and the full suite runs 1093 tests with 1 skipped.

groups.title: Documentation
intro: The prune paragraph in docs/cli.md now says that prune removes only folders, and that a file or a link where it looks for worktrees is listed as kept.

files.note: Replaces the sentence about unlinking a link with the folders-only rule.
